# Blackline 0.15.52 — attachments become a cache, pictures get a middle size

Built 18 September 2026 on Derek's machine. Installs over any earlier build and keeps its data.

**Wire protocol 6: both sides must be on 0.15.52 or later.** A peer on an older build is refused at
the handshake and simply appears offline, in both directions — deliberately, so two clients never
half-understand each other. If somebody you talk to has not updated, neither of you will see the
other until they do.

The store schema moves to version 9. The upgrade is in place and keeps everything; there is nothing
to export first.

Still **not code-signed**: SmartScreen → More info → Run anyway.

## Storage stops being a wall

Reaching your storage limit used to refuse the transfer — "over your storage limit" — which meant a
person who filled it in month four stopped being able to receive files at all. Attachments are
content-addressed, so the bytes can go while the message stays, and that is what happens now.

* At the limit, the files you have gone longest without opening have their **bytes dropped** to make
  room. Their messages are untouched: the name, the size, the thumbnail and the offer to fetch it
  again all survive.
* **Keep** marks a file to stay. Every file says which it is — *Kept*, *Cached*, or *Yours* — on the
  file itself, so you can tell at a glance which of yours are safe.
* **A file you sent is never dropped**, without your marking it. If you drop it and the person you
  sent it to drops theirs, it is gone from the world; no server has a third copy.
* If everything left is kept or yours, the store goes over the limit on purpose rather than lose
  something, and Settings → Files says by how much.
* The one thing still refused is a single file larger than your whole allowance, because no amount
  of room can be made for it. The message says both numbers.
* Asking for a file that has been dropped on the other side now says **they no longer have it**,
  rather than looking like a refusal.

Measured: a client with room for four files took forty without refusing one.

## Pictures travel at the size you actually look at them

A thumbnail is 40px and rides with the message; the original can be megabytes. Scrolling an old
conversation means looking at pictures at *screen* size, which is neither, so the sender now makes a
third: about 100 KB at 1024px, sent as its own attachment and fetched when a picture comes into
view.

Measured between two machines: twelve 3 MB pictures cost **1.2 MB instead of 36 MB**, and no
original was fetched. The original is still one tap away, and the viewer says which size you are
looking at rather than pretending.

Pictures sent by older builds have no middle size and cannot be given one — making it would mean
fetching the original, which is the whole cost it exists to avoid.

## Spaces

* **View channels** is a permission now, per space and per channel, with the same
  deny / neutral / allow control as every other channel permission. It is not a hidden row: a role
  denied it comes off the channel's readers, so the channel's key is not theirs and its words cannot
  be opened by any client. Denying it to `@everyone` on one channel is what makes that channel
  private.
* A space invite in its short form — `@name/code` — can be pasted into **Join a space**. It could
  always be accepted; the box just would not take it.
* The private-channel switch says why it cannot be turned on when a space has no roles yet, instead
  of refusing silently.

## Calls

* **Remote control has a switch.** "Allow them to ask for control" sits under Share system audio in
  your own stream's menu. It is true only while you are actually sharing and false the moment you
  stop, and the core drops the request when it is off — so the switch is enforced where a modified
  client cannot reach it. Granting is still a separate question, answered live, ended instantly by
  the stop key.
* The speaking ring no longer thins out when somebody is sharing a screen or a camera. It was being
  painted underneath the picture.
* Its green is now Discord's, and it is its own colour rather than the status green doing two jobs.
* The call timer updates everywhere at once. Only the dock's own clock was ticking; the others sat
  at whatever they were drawn with until something forced a redraw.
* The LIVE badge is gone.

## Fixes

* **"Keep this link relayed" could be switched on and never came back on.** The setting travels as
  `relay_only` and the interface read `relayOnly`, which is nothing at all — no error, no warning,
  just a switch that would not stick.
* **A recovery file this build wrote, it would then refuse to read.** The writer moved to version 4
  for space identities and the check that opens one still accepted 3. Fixed before anyone met it.
* Your profile picture now updates everywhere the moment you change it — every message you have
  sent, your tile in a call, the member lists — instead of only the corner it is set in.
* The add-people button appears in group chats and adds to the group you are in; from a direct chat
  it still makes a group.
* A space's colour is the same colour wherever it is drawn. There were three recipes and they had
  drifted.
* The two Hue sliders in Appearance are the same control drawn the same way.
* On a direct row, the time and the close button sit on the row's centre line.

## What this build does not do

* Nothing here recovers a file whose bytes were dropped, or gives an old picture a middle size.
  These change what happens from now on.
* Sealing a space's member records — so members cannot learn each other's addresses — is half built
  and cannot be switched on. It is not offered anywhere in the interface.
* The account key is still held by every device of an account. Adding a device still means a
  recovery file with a passphrase, so nothing hands a stolen device the power to revoke your others;
  moving the key off devices is the work that comes with MLS.
